newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S BOURSE RESUMES ITS UPWARD TREND.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S BOURSE RESUMES ITS UPWARD TREND.

text.p: Morocco's bourse ended its Wednesday session 0.34 percent higher, pushed up by active trading in blue-chip firms, including BMCE Bank, brokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 656.78 points from 654.58 points on the previous session.
"The stock market index returned to its rising trend as expected...Traders continue to invest in blue-chip firms such as BMCE and Wafabank," a broker at Upline Securities said.
The index rose over 46 percent performance since the beginning of the year, the broker said.
BMCE rose five dirhams to 575 dirhams, the broker said, adding that more than 3,000 BMCE shares exchanged hands on Wednesday.
Wafabank continued its rising trend to close at 865 dirhams against 861 dirhams in the previous session.
Morocco's main oil refinery Samir and second largest private conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement both rose five dirhams to 335 and 760 dirhams, respectively.
ONA Group remained unchanged at 832 dirhams. ONA, which holds interests in more than 80 firms, has a market capitalisation of more than 14 billion dirhams.
Its subsidiary Centrale Laitiere, rose eight dirhams to close at 2,758 dirhams.
Total trading volume fell to 61.1 million dirhams from 74.6 million dirhams on Tuesday. Exchanges through the electronic trading system represented 5.9 million dirhams, a stockbroker said.
Only five stocks, among them BMCE and Samir were introduced in the new system launched earlier this year, out of a total 49 listed firms on the 68-year old Casablanca bourse, the stockbroker added.
